N-3.10-A.skill: count the solutions of a trigonometric equation with a changed input coefficient on an interval, avoiding lost or extra solutions (including the single-solution case sin u = 1).

N-3.10-B.skill: solve a trigonometric inequality on an interval, keeping every arc and reversing the inequality when dividing by a negative.

N-3.11-A.skill: find the range of a transformed secant or cosecant function by combining the |value| ≥ 1 restriction with a stretch, reflection and shift.

N-3.11-B.skill: locate every vertical asymptote of a secant or cosecant graph with a horizontal compression and phase shift, on a given interval.

N-3.12-A.skill: identify the one invalid identity among four by recognizing which algebraic or trigonometric shortcut fails (square root, sign under a shift, missing cross term, missing factor).

N-3.12-B.skill: apply the double-angle identity after recovering the missing ratio and its sign from the quadrant, avoiding the cos 2θ and missing-factor traps.

N-3.13-A.skill: convert a rectangular point to polar form with a required negative radius, choosing the direction opposite to the point's quadrant.

N-3.13-B.skill: recognize which polar pair names the same point as a given pair with a negative radius, adjusting the angle by π when the sign of r flips.

N-3.14-A.skill: describe a rose curve from its equation: petal count (n or 2n), petal length (amplitude) and tip direction (sine versus cosine).

N-3.14-B.skill: classify a limaçon or cardioid from its equation using the ratio of the constant to the coefficient, and find its axis of symmetry and farthest distance from the pole.

N-3.15-A.skill: decide where a polar point moves toward the pole by comparing the signs of r and dr/dθ, rather than the sign of dr/dθ alone.

N-3.15-B.skill: compute the average rate of change of a signed polar radius and interpret it together with the sign of r, including when r crosses the pole.
